source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: Premature broad abnormal QRS-T complexes occur without a preceding P wave or without a related P wave.
QRS duration usually exceeds 120 ms; T polarity is usually opposite to the dominant QRS deflection.
The pause is often fully compensatory; coupling is measured from QRS onset.
Bigeminy alternates sinus and premature beats; trigeminy has one premature beat after every two sinus beats (printed-page 477 terminology).
Different morphologies and coupling intervals in the same lead illustrate multifocal beats; different morphologies with fixed coupling are termed polymorphic (printed-page 477 terminology).
An interpolated premature beat lies between two adjacent normal sinus beats without a subsequent compensatory pause (printed-page 477 terminology).

authored_choices.morphology: Reuses broad QRS and discordant T from VentricularEscapeTables only where the original ordinal modulo 4 equals 3. Reusing morphology does not reuse escape timing or locate the same ectopic focus.
authored_choices.sinusSlots: The final slot of this fixed example emits no atrial electrical/mechanical events; the next sinus P occurs at 3200 ms. No sinus-node reset is inferred, and this does not assert that all PVCs lack independent P waves.

groupedVariants.shared: Coupling is 500 ms and the compensatory pause is 1100 ms. The final slot has no atrial events; morphology/amplitude match the original monomorphic example.

diverseVariants.morphologyA: Original ventricular tables: QRS 160 ms, QT 480 ms and T 220 ms.
diverseVariants.morphologyB: Original ventricular electrode QRS/T potentials are inverted. QRS is linearly extended to 180 ms, T is delayed by 20 ms, and QT/T are 500/220 ms. This is an explicitly authored morphology, not anatomical calibration of another ectopic focus.
diverseVariants.mechanics: A ventricular mechanical event follows each QRS by 80 ms. Morphology polarity does not change ejection direction or amplitude.

interpolatedVariant.pOverlay: The next sinus P at 3000-3100 ms independently overlaps the PVC T at 2920-3140 ms. QRS occurs at its original time of 3160 ms.
interpolatedVariant.reason: The authored rate is 60/min so that the full 480 ms PVC QT ends before the next sinus QRS, without shortening or truncating existing T. PR prolongation and concealed conduction are not modeled.

coupletVariant.reason: Two identical broad QRS/discordant T complexes each retain the full 480 ms QT and return to baseline 20 ms before the second PVC. Intervals of 500/500/1400 ms are authored and do not establish general compensatory-pause rules, VT or refractory behavior. Neither PVC slot emits atrial events.

polymorphicCoupletVariant.timing: Identical to the monomorphic couplet: five slots over 4000 ms, QRS at 2260/2760 ms, and intervals of 500/500/1400 ms.
polymorphicCoupletVariant.morphologyA: First PVC: QRS 160 ms, QT 480 ms and T 220 ms.
polymorphicCoupletVariant.morphologyB: Only the second PVC uses the existing inverted-potential authored transformation with QRS/QT/T of 180/500/220 ms.
polymorphicCoupletVariant.mechanics: Each mechanical event remains QRS + 80 ms, with ejection direction/amplitude matching the monomorphic couplet. Potential polarity does not imply pressure changes.

ronTLongQtVariant.composition: Only slot 2's repolarization band is extended. Its QRS and other sinus P/QRS/T remain unchanged; the long T and PVC QRS add as potentials. This is a teaching signal combination, not a tissue-repolarization reset or vulnerable-period model.
ronTLongQtVariant.mechanics: Retains the original monomorphic PVC mechanical timing, ejection and pressure; no automatic VT/VF generation.

shortCoupledRonTVariant.mechanics: Triggered 80 ms after QRS. All beats in the short-coupled mode share the same short ejection/pulse parameters, without beatwise filling, low-amplitude PVC, post-extrasystolic potentiation or stroke-volume feedback.
shortCoupledRonTVariant.composition: The original sinus T and early PVC add as potentials. QT is not prolonged; no refractory period is inferred and VT/VF is not triggered automatically.

implementation: Group lengths 2/3/4 serve existing monomorphic sequences. The five-slot couplet uses normal/PVC masks 7/24. Eight-slot polymorphic/multifocal examples use normal/A/B masks 119/8/128. The original index is group*count+slot.
Modes share a bounded indexed accessor supplying actual mechanical events to the timeline and pressure. No new atrial event kind is added.
Half-open intervals, exact budgets, original group*count+slot indexing and bounded-lookback recovery; no replay from the epoch.
Twelve-lead and monitor lead II share a source. The QRS summary explicitly verifies sinus slot 0 only.
Both demos load fixed examples and reset previous parameters, supporting direct switching and atomic rejection. Other physiological channels use actual ventricular/respiratory events.
Group length drives event timing, morphology masks, pressure access and recovery. AV conduction ratios are not used to simulate bigeminy/trigeminy.

Slots 3/7 of the eight-slot group are PVCs without atrial events. The multifocal example delays only slot 7 by 100 ms; pressure and bounded lookback share this schedule. Reversed polarity is not treated as negative ejection.

The interpolated example uses a three-second group and four-beat index. The atrial clock remains at 1000 ms and the PVC is extra slot 3. Its baseline rate of 60/min and the other examples' 75/min are separately constrained by configuration factories and timeline validation.
limitations: Specific durations, amplitudes and one PVC after every three sinus beats are authored parameters, not traced textbook measurements.

Fixed monomorphic, bigeminy/trigeminy, dual-morphology fixed/variable-coupling, interpolated and monomorphic/dual-morphology couplet examples are implemented. Fixed R-on-T examples with long QT and with normal QT plus short coupling are implemented. Other coupling, couplet and remaining variants are unimplemented.
No automatic ectopic-focus, retrograde-conduction, fusion, concealed-conduction, refractory or sinus-node mechanism.
Mechanical events occur early without modeling beatwise filling/stroke volume, PVC pulse deficit or post-extrasystolic potentiation. Ventricular mechanics can be explicitly disabled.
VT/SVT and other ECG, respiratory, perfusion and artifact work remain open; dynamic UI rulers are deferred.
Windows behavior is not yet manually verified; native automated regression checks cover the implemented behavior.

summary: A ventricular couplet consists of two consecutive PVCs with no intervening normal beat. The source does not supply this example's timing or hemodynamic parameters.
Section 4.17.3.1 of the 2024 guideline allows identical or different PVC morphologies within a couplet. It does not supply this example's parameters or anatomical localization.
R-on-T means that the PVC R wave falls on the preceding T wave. The source does not supply this example's local QT or mechanistic parameters.
